1.5a — Movement II: Speed, deltaTime & Tuning

The movement works; today you make it feel right. That means understanding where speed actually lives — the code, or the Inspector — and why deltaTime is the difference between a game and a slideshow.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the top of PlayerController.cs again:

[SerializeField] private float xSpeed = 5.0f;
[SerializeField] private float ySpeed = 5.0f;

Predict: you press Play, change xSpeed in the Inspector to 12, stop, and open the file. What number is in the code now? Then you close Play, set it to 12 in edit mode, and open the file again — what is in the code now, and what is in the Inspector?

The two answers are different, and the difference is the whole point of [SerializeField]: the code holds a default; the scene/prefab holds an override that beats the default. The Inspector is data saved in your scene file, not in your .cs file.

Socratic

Your fork of the starter has xSpeed = 5 in the code. If your friend clones your repo and opens the Overworld, do they see your Inspector override or the code default — and why does git never see the Inspector value at all?

Build Lab ~25 min

Feel pass, one value at a time. Designers do not guess good numbers, they tune them — one variable, one playtest, repeat:

  1. Set xSpeed to 3. Walk across the Overworld. Too slow? Probably.
  2. Try 5, then 8. Fill in a mini-table as you go: speed / how it feels / one adjective.
  3. Pick the winner in edit mode, so it saves. Do the same for ySpeed — should it match xSpeed, or is the overworld nicer slightly slower on the vertical? Decide, do not default.
Why the Inspector and not the code? Because the point of a tuning knob is turning it while the game runs. If you had to stop, edit code, wait for compile, and re-press play for every number, you would tune three values a day. This way you tune thirty.

Now break deltaTime on purpose. In PlayerController.Update, temporarily delete * Time.deltaTime from the xVector line. Play on this machine; then run the same build on a different machine if you can.

Bug Hunt: The frame-rate bug

  1. With deltaTime removed, about how many times per second does Update run on this machine? (Your PlayerLogger from 1.3a can count it.)
  2. If Update ran 240 times a second on a friend's gaming monitor, how much faster would the player be — and what does that do to "fair" in a game?
  3. Put deltaTime back. Where does the per-frame speed get divided down to per-second, exactly?
Tinker ~15 min

Tinker: Diagonal, again, for real

  1. Set xSpeed and ySpeed to 8 and walk in a circle. Now hold A + W together: is the diagonal faster than the straight lines? Time it across the screen both ways.
  2. The fix is normalization — dividing the vector by its length so the diagonal matches. The starter does not do it for the player. Where WILL you meet normalization this semester — which NPC moves toward you at a constant speed no matter the angle?
  3. Change the code default of xSpeed to your tuned winner number and commit. Which file did you actually change — and does the Inspector override still beat it?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain Inspector override vs code default and where each is stored
  • Tune a speed value in play mode, then persist it in edit mode
  • Explain what Time.deltaTime does and demonstrate the bug without it
  • Say what normalization is for, even though you have not written it yet
